blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings was little changed, 92 in June and 93 in September (+1.1%), and it took 8.3% of the city’s 351 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 147 in June to 128 in September (−12.9%), and it took 14.2% of the city’s 591 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Sullivan Station for detached houses in September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, August (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Sullivan Station

items.t: Fee-simple detached lots — the land form that actually trades: A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees; diligence is title, zone, SSMUH band and any riparian area on the parcel. South Newton lands carry R-series residential zones, with RA at the rural edges toward Colebrook, under Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000.

Lot sizes, only as the research states them: subdivision lots follow the Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 zone minimums for the lot's R-series zone; a Sullivan Station lot-size statistic is UNVERIFIED, and no typical lot size is invented here.
Bare-land strata: none verified
Strata attached ground — cross-reference only, never re-counted

Assemblies / development sites: The documented development frame is plan-led: the rescinded South Newton plan no longer governs, designations were updated by Corporate Report R246 (endorsed December 2, 2024), and any site's potential is read off the Surrey 2050 OCP and Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, not off the old NCP.
ALR vs non-ALR split: No ALR acreage or split figure for the sub-area is stated: UNVERIFIED.

Servicing: properties not connected to community water and sewer are among the exemptions from Surrey's SSMUH allowances — which is itself the servicing signal for a land buyer here: a lot's connection position changes what it can carry.
55+ position: No 55+ item is imported here as lot stock.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Sullivan Station

items.t: Municipality and community: City of Surrey, in the Newton community. "Sullivan Station" is the SnapStats / board sub-area name for Surrey in the September 2026 report; the City does not publish a separate "Sullivan Station" plan boundary — the City names in this ground are "Sullivan," "Sullivan Heights" and "South Newton," and a City boundary line for Sullivan Station itself is UNVERIFIED. The City's South Newton page describes South Newton as a large neighbourhood within the southeast of the broader Newton community, with neighbourhood commercial nodes including Panorama Heights at 152 Street and Hwy 10 and Sullivan Heights at 64 Ave and 144 Street — the Sullivan Station board sub-area sits inside that South Newton ground.

Plan ground: the South Newton plan area is approximately 485 hectares (1,200 acres), generally located north of Hwy 10, east of King George Boulevard and west of 152 Street, bordered by the East Newton NCPs to the northwest. Nearby areas: Panorama Ridge (south), East Newton (northwest), West Newton (west), Cloverdale (east, across the 152 Street side).

Plan status — read before relying on any older plan document: the South Newton plan was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update and is no longer in effect; development in this area is led by the Official Community Plan, and on December 2, 2024 Council endorsed Corporate Report R246, which updated land use designations to reflect current market conditions.
SD36 runs K–7 elementary and 8–12 secondary, with no middle-school tier.

Creeks: South Newton is home to several important fish-bearing creeks, including the headwaters of Archibald Creek, Sullivan Heights Creek and several tributaries of Hyland Creek — riparian/setback rules can therefore apply to creek-side lots in this ground.

Transit: buses on the 152 St and 64 Ave corridors serve this ground — route 321 runs via 152 St and King George Blvd, and route 322 runs via 132 St and 64 Ave between Newton and Scottsdale; the R1 RapidBus runs on King George Boulevard west of the area between Newton Exchange and King George Station via Surrey Central Station. No SkyTrain station is inside Sullivan Station. Route-level confirmation for a specific Sullivan Station street: UNVERIFIED against a TransLink timetable.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Sullivan Station

items.t: Zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs: South Newton lands carry R-series residential zones, with RA at the rural edges toward Colebrook; a parcel's zone and its subdivision minimums are read off the bylaw for that zone.

SSMUH — Surrey's bands, as the City states them: a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop; the BC Building Code permits one secondary suite per house; properties not connected to community water and sewer are among the exemptions. The City also states the SSMUH changes do NOT retroactively legalize a secondary suite or coach house built without permits — an existing unpermitted suite still needs the permit and approval process, so verify suite permits on any listing here.

Riparian / creek rules: Archibald Creek headwaters, Sullivan Heights Creek and Hyland Creek tributaries run through South Newton, and riparian/setback requirements can limit building envelopes on creek-side lots — check City mapping before valuing an addition, a rebuild or an SSMUH scheme on a creek-side parcel.

ALR block — stated for completeness, for any parcel where ALR status is confirmed on the ALC maps: ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; caps: principal residence ≤500 m², suite within the principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm-class thresholds in the full three-tier form ($2,500 at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

Bare-land strata block — stated for completeness, governing no Sullivan Station stock verified here: where a bare-land strata lot does exist in BC, it is strata tenure — Form B (SPA s. 59) within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid age bylaw.

Surrey property taxes / holding cost: City of Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty if not paid by midnight July 2 and a further 5% penalty after September 2 — city-wide figures, not area-specific; no area-specific levy for Sullivan Station was found on a City source: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sullivan Station

items.t: The plan most sellers still name no longer exists. The South Newton plan was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — a Sullivan Station lot marketed "per the South Newton NCP" is marketed off a dead plan, and the live frame is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900) plus the R246 designation updates of December 2, 2024. This is the single most consequential land fact in the sub-area.
A new school redrew the catchment questions in January 2026.

The 280 m² line is a value line. Surrey's SSMUH bands step at 280 m² / 281 m² and again at frequent-bus-stop proximity — two near-identical teardown lots on the same Sullivan Station street can carry different unit counts, and the difference is measurable off the lot's surveyed area and the bus-stop map before an offer is written.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Sullivan Station than in June?
faq.a: In Sullivan Station, listings of houses was little changed, 92 in June and 93 in September (+1.1%); condos and townhomes fell from 147 in June to 128 in September (−12.9%).

faq.q: How big is Sullivan Station compared with the rest of Surrey?
faq.a: In September 2026, Sullivan Station held 8.3% of the 1,120 houses listed in Surrey and 8.4% of the 1,523 condos and townhomes listed in Surrey.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Sullivan Station from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 29 houses and 84 condos and townhomes sold in Sullivan Station over those 4 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Sullivan Station?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Sullivan Station?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Is there a bare-land subdivision or lot release in Sullivan Station?
faq.a: What trades as land is individual fee-simple detached lots under the R-series zones.

faq.q: What plan governs a Sullivan Station lot now?
faq.a: The Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900) and Zoning Bylaw No. 12000. The South Newton plan that covered this ground was rescinded and is no longer in effect, and designations were updated by Corporate Report R246 (endorsed December 2, 2024). Never plan off Bylaw 18020 as a current OCP.

faq.q: How many units can a Sullivan Station house lot carry?
faq.a: Confirm the lot's band and bus-stop eligibility with the City before valuing a teardown or builder sale — and note an unpermitted existing suite is not legalized by the changes.

faq.q: Do creek rules really affect ordinary lots here?
faq.a: They can: Archibald Creek headwaters, Sullivan Heights Creek and Hyland Creek tributaries run through South Newton, and riparian/setback requirements can limit the building envelope on a creek-side lot. Check City mapping before valuing an addition or rebuild.
